claim: Cassis harbour boat tours come in four sightseeing circuits — 3 calanques (1h, €21), 5 calanques (1h20, €25), 8 calanques (1h50, €29), 9 calanques (2h20, €33) — plus a 3-calanques + swim-stop option at €40 for 2h, reserved for swimmers.
quote: 3 calanques (1:00h) - €21.00 ... 5 calanques (1:20h) - €25.00 ... 8 calanques (1:50h) - €29.00 ... 9 calanques (2h20) - €33.00 ... 3 calanquess + relaxation stop (2:00h) - €40.00 ... reserved for people who know how to swim

claim: From La Ciotat, the main calanque-tour operator is Les Amis des Calanques at quai Ganteaume, running from 4 April to 11 November 2026.
quote: AMIS DES CALANQUES ... Address: quai Ganteaume ... Opening: from 4 April to 11 November 2026

claim: In 2026 the national park requires a free prior reservation to enter Sugiton and Pierres Tombées on 20–21 June, daily from 27 June to 30 August, and on 5–6 and 12–13 September; bookings open 11 June 2026 at 09:00 CET, up to 3 days ahead, max 5 people per slot.
quote: 20-21 June, everyday from 27 June to 30 August, on 5-6 September and on 12-13 September 2026 ... Reservations will open on 11 June 2026 at 9:00 am CET ... Group reservations available for up to 5 people

claim: Outside of Sugiton, the Cassis calanques remain free to enter, but a daily fire-risk alert level dictates access — on RED days the massif is closed all day, with the forecast updated at 6 p.m. for the following day from June to September.
quote: Mid-June to mid-September : prior reservation for access ONLY for the SUGITON calanque in Marseille ... The other calanques of the national park are free of access ... RED level ... access PROHIBITED all day ... Updated at 6pm for the following day (JUNE TO SEPTEMBER)

claim: The classic Cassis hike follows the red-and-white GR98-51 markings from Port-Miou to Port-Pin (2.3 km, 30 min, easy) then on to En-Vau (3.8 km, 1h15 one-way, medium), with a steep slippery descent into En-Vau where hikers may need their hands; the Gorguettes car park feeds a €1.60 shuttle into Cassis in summer.
quote: The path follows the itinerary of the GR98-51 trail ... 2,3km (30min) ... 3,8km (1h15) ... Easy until Port min / Medium for En-vau ... In the descent to En-vau valley, don't hesitate to use your hands ... parking des Gorguettes ... only 1€60 the round trip

claim: Cap Canaille between Cassis and La Ciotat rises to 394 m and is the highest sea cliff in France, with the Corniche/Route des Crêtes scenic road running across the top.
quote: At 394 m (1,293 ft), it is the highest sea cliff of France ... The Corniche des Crêtes scenic road runs over the top of the cliff

claim: The Soubeyranes cliffs at Cap Canaille sit inside the Calanques National Park; the Route des Crêtes provides multiple lookouts but is automatically closed on red fire-risk days from 1 June to 30 September, and the park warns against approaching the cliff edge.
quote: The breathtaking Soubeyranes cliffs between Cassis and La Ciotat are among the highest in Europe ... automatically closed on days classified as red for fire danger between 1 June and 30 September ... when stopping on Route des Crêtes, do not approach the edge. Sudden wind can cause falls

claim: Île Verte, just off La Ciotat, is the only wooded island in the Calanques National Park; visitors reach it by shuttle from the Old Port (April–October), can walk a one-hour loop, and swim from two small calanques (La Plageolle and Seynerolles).
quote: Just a few hundred metres from the coast of La Ciotat, Ile Verte is the only wooded island in the Calanques National Park ... It is only possible to swim offshore from two calanques on the island (La Plageolle in the north and Seynerolles in the south)

claim: The Aquilade maritime shuttle to Île Verte leaves the Old Port of La Ciotat for a 10-minute crossing; in July–August 2026 it runs hourly 09:00–18:00, with adult return €14 and child (under 10) €9.
quote: Departing from the old port of La Ciotat, the Aquilade maritime shuttle makes the 10-minute crossing ... 09:00 - 18:00 ... Every hour ... Adults : Return ticket price €14 ... Children under 10 years old: €9 return fare

claim: Calanque de Figuerolles in La Ciotat is reached on foot from the Vieux-Port via avenues des Calanques, du Mugel and de Figuerolles, descending a small staircase to a beach with very good water quality.
quote: walk along the quays of the Port-Vieux and, after passing the Avenue des Calanques, avenue du Mugel, then Avenue of Figuerolles ... you reach the creek by a charming little staircase ... The calanque offers a beautiful beach and water of very good quality

claim: Plage du Bestouan, just west of Cassis, is a pebble beach within the Calanques landscape with clear turquoise water for long swims, calmer and shallower than Cassis's Grande-Mer beach, with supervised swimming daily from 15 June to 16 September.
quote: a delightful pebble beach among the Calanques, in whose crystal clear turquoise waters you can take long swims ... it is smaller than the Grande-Mer beach, but offers a calmer setting and shallower water ... Supervised swimming runs from 9am to 7pm ... every day from June 15 to September 16
